newsitem.title: USA: Mortgage rates barely changed in week -- FHLMC.
newsitem.headline: Mortgage rates barely changed in week -- FHLMC.

text.p: Home mortgage rates were barely changed this week, the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corp. said Thursday.
Thirty-year fixed-rate mortgages averaged 7.88 percent, up slightly from 7.85 percent last week, while 15-year mortgages rose to 7.38 percent from 7.35 percent.
One-year adjustable mortgage rates inched down to an average of 5.55 percent from 5.57 percent.
A year ago, the 30-year rate averaged 7.02 percent, the 15-year 6.52 percent and the adjustable loan 5.37 percent.

"Steady interest rates are a reflection of the general consensus that the economy is not expanding too quickly, therefore the Federal Reserve Board will most probably not make any moves to raise rates when it meets next Tuesday," said Robert Van Order, Freddie Mac chief economist.
"Comparatively low mortgage rates and low inflation combine to help make this a very affordable time for those who are planning to invest in a home."
On Friday the Commerce Department will issue U.S. December single-family home sales data. The Fed's policy-setting Federal Open Market Committee will meet Feb. 4 and 5.

Freddie Mac said lenders charged an average of 1.8 percent in fees and points on 30-year loans, unchanged from last week. They charged 1.7 percent on 15-year mortgages, down from 1.8 percent last week, and 1.4 percent on adjustable loans, unchanged from last week.
